markup:
For most houses, I’d recommend a **20–40 kWh home battery backup system** if you want to keep most household appliances running during a power outage. If you only need essentials, 10–15 kWh may be enough.

The right size depends on **how much electricity you use, what you want to power, and how long you want the backup to last.**

## Typical home battery sizes

| Backup goal | Battery capacity | Approximate runtime |
|---|---:|---|
| Essentials: fridge, Wi-Fi, lights | 5–10 kWh | 12–24 hours |
| Essentials plus some appliances | 10–20 kWh | 12–24 hours |
| Most of the house | 20–40 kWh | 12–24 hours |
| Whole house, including AC | 40–80+ kWh | 12–24 hours |

These are rough estimates. Electric heating, air conditioning, EV charging, and other large loads can dramatically shorten runtime.

## Calculate your battery size

A simple formula is:

\[
\text{Battery size (kWh)}=\frac{\text{Daily usage (kWh)}\times\text{Backup days}}{0.9}
\]

The 0.9 factor allows for approximately 10% of energy being unavailable due to system losses.

For example, if your home consumes 30 kWh per day:

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  {@body const [daily,setDaily] = DIL.useState(30)}
  {@body const [days,setDays] = DIL.useState(1)}
  <text weight="medium">Home battery sizing calculator</text>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Electricity usage per day</text>
    **{daily} kWh**
  </row>
  <slider min={5} max={100} step={5} value={daily} onChange={setDaily}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Days of backup</text>
    **{days} {days===1?"day":"days"}**
  </row>
  <slider min={1} max={5} step={1} value={days} onChange={setDays}/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" padding={3} radius="lg" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated battery capacity needed</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{Math.ceil(daily*days/0.9)} kWh</title>
    <caption>Assumes no solar recharging and 90% usable energy efficiency. Actual requirements depend on loads and system specifications.</caption>
  </box>
</box>

{@body const [duration,setDuration] = DIL.useState("24 hours")}
{@body const [loads,setLoads] = DIL.useState("most")}
{@body const [solar,setSolar] = DIL.useState("no")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Size my home battery backup. Monthly electricity usage: "+usage+". Desired outage duration: "+duration+". Loads to back up: "+loads+". Solar panels: "+solar+". Recommend kWh capacity, power output in kW, and approximate number of batteries.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>1. How much electricity do you use monthly?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={usage} onChange={setUsage}>
        <radio value="under 500 kWh">Under 500 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="500–1000 kWh">500–1,000 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="1000–2000 kWh">1,000–2,000 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="over 2000 kWh">Over 2,000 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>2. How long should the backup last?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>
        <radio value="12 hours">12 hours</radio>
        <radio value="24 hours">24 hours</radio>
        <radio value="48 hours">48 hours</radio>
        <radio value="72+ hours">3+ days</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>3. What do you want to power?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={loads} onChange={setLoads}>
        <radio value="essentials">Essentials only (fridge, lights, internet)</radio>
        <radio value="most">Most of the house, including AC</radio>
        <radio value="all">Everything, including large appliances</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>4. Do you have solar panels?</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={solar} onChange={setSolar}>
        <radio value="yes">Yes</radio>
        <radio value="no">No</radio>
        <radio value="planning">Planning to</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate my recommended battery size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With those answers, I can estimate both the **battery capacity (kWh)** and the **power output (kW)** you need. The latter is especially important if you want to run central AC, electric ovens, or other high-power appliances during an outage.
